tasks.task: Establish site setup, scaffold access routes, and occupant protocols
tasks.scope: Mobilise plant, confirm scaffold access via Kiora Lane and courtyard, establish exclusion zones below balconies, brief occupants on work schedule and access restrictions, confirm utilities isolation points.
hazards: Trip hazard from plant and scaffold components on access routes
Vehicle strike on workers during plant mobilisation in courtyard and Kiora Lane
Occupant confusion or non-compliance with exclusion zones leading to injury from falling objects
Utility strike during isolation point confirmation
tasks.dominant_hazard: Vehicle strike during plant mobilisation in shared courtyard
controls: Establish vehicle exclusion zone in courtyard and Kiora Lane — signage, barricades, or traffic controller present during all plant movement.
Brief all site workers and occupants on courtyard vehicle movement times — confirm understanding before plant mobilisation starts.
Clear and tape all trip hazards on access routes before scaffold erection — cables, components, debris must not cross walkways.
Establish exclusion zones below all balconies and elevated work areas — barricade perimeter, post warning signs, brief occupants on no-access rule.
Identify and mark all known utility routes before isolation confirmation — stop work if route condition differs from plan.
Brief all occupants on work schedule, access restrictions, and exclusion zones — provide written notice, confirm receipt.
Notify building occupants / body corporate / strata manager of work schedule, access restrictions, and expected noise/dust at least 48 hours before work starts
hold_points: ⚠️ HOLD POINT — do not mobilise plant until: vehicle exclusion zone is physically barricaded and traffic controller (if required) is on site.
⚠️ HOLD POINT — do not start work until: written notification delivered to all affected occupants and body corporate/strata manager
stop_work: 🛑 STOP WORK if: vehicle enters exclusion zone during plant mobilisation or any worker or occupant enters barricaded exclusion zone below balconies.
🛑 STOP WORK if: occupant confusion or breach of exclusion zone protocol occurs or access route trip hazards reappear during work.
🛑 STOP WORK if: occupant balcony below work zone is not closed and barricaded

Vegetation trimmed away from surfaces designated for painting or remedial works prior to commencement — area excluded if vegetation impedes access
On-site parking or provision of parking permits required for duration of works

Hard hat — all personnel within plant mobilisation zone and below scaffold work areas.

tasks.task: Erect scaffold over balconies to engineer specification
tasks.scope: Install scaffold from courtyard and Kiora Lane access, secure to building facade, install guardrails and edge protection, confirm bearing and load paths, certify installation ready for load.
tasks.hrcw_category: cl.2 — Construction work at height — risk of fall >2m
hazards: Fall from height during scaffold erection above 4m
Collapse of scaffold due to inadequate bearing or load path on facade
Fall of tools or materials from scaffold onto workers or occupants below
Entrapment or struck-by hazard during scaffold component handling and fixing
Unsuitable surface for load attachment — facade failure under load
tasks.dominant_hazard: Collapse of scaffold due to inadequate bearing or load path on building facade
controls: Obtain engineer's scaffold design and load calculation before any component arrives on site. Verify bearing points, fixing method, and load path to facade. Store design on point of use.

Check all facade bearing surfaces (concrete, masonry, mortar joint condition) are sound and capable of stated load. Identify and record any cracking, spalling, or cavity. Do not proceed if bearing is unsuitable — contact engineer.
Install facade tie-down fixings only to locations and depth specified by engineer. Use only fixings and fasteners named in design. Verify fixing centres match drawing before load is applied.
Erect scaffold in sequence specified by engineer. Install base plates, standards, ledgers, and ties in correct order. Do not skip steps or alter sequence without engineer approval.

Install guardrails and toe boards as scaffold is erected — do not leave any level unprotected during construction. Height of guardrail must be 950–1150 mm above platform. No gaps larger than 120 mm between rails or platform.

Install safety netting or catch screens on all sides below scaffold where work is above occupied balconies or communal areas. Mesh size 40–50 mm. Secure netting at top and sides to prevent tools or materials falling onto occupants.

Barricade access to courtyard and Kiora Lane directly below scaffold. Post exclusion zone signage. Prohibit entry to anyone without harness and spotter approval. Warn all building occupants before scaffold work commences.

Appoint a site spotter with clear line of sight to all erection activities. Spotter must remain on ground during all lifting and fixing. Use two-way radio or hand signal protocol — no solo erection work at height.
hold_points: ⚠️ HOLD POINT — do not apply load or permit worker access until: Licensed scaffolder and engineer check scaffold installation, verify all tie-downs and bearings match specification, and sign handover certificate.
⚠️ HOLD POINT — do not start erection until: Engineer approves facade bearing assessment report and confirms facade is suitable to carry stated loads.
stop_work: 🛑 STOP WORK if: Facade bearing surface shows new cracking, spalling, cavity, or subsidence during or after tie-down installation.
🛑 STOP WORK if: Any tie-down fixing does not achieve full depth, backing, or torque specified by engineer, or fastener is loose or damaged.
🛑 STOP WORK if: Guardrails, toe boards, or safety netting become damaged, dislodged, or incomplete at any level.
🛑 STOP WORK if: occupant balcony below work zone is not closed and barricaded

Obtain working-at-heights permit signed by supervisor before elevated work commences.

Obtain and display handover certificate from licenced scaffolder before any worker uses completed scaffold.
tell all building occupants 2 working days before scaffold work. Advise of exclusion zone below scaffold and expected noise and activity.
Maintain a daily erection log: date, time, weather, workers present, components installed, engineer communications, any issues or delays.
Keep engineer's design drawing, load calculation, and tie-down schedule accessible on site throughout erection and use.

Notify affected residents before any noise/dust generating work on their level or adjacent levels

monitoring.frequency: Before handover; daily during erection; immediately after weather or structural event
monitoring.evidence: Handover certificate signed; hold point inspection photos; daily log; engineer sign-off on design compliance

responsibility.SUP: Verify scaffold or EWP certification, supervise erection, sign off load checks

tasks.task: Remove existing tile bed, screed, membrane, and associated fittings
tasks.scope: Strip tiles, grout, and screed from all balconies; remove failed waterproofing membrane; lift and isolate balustrade panels; stockpile debris below scaffold; manage silica dust control during removal.
hazards: Silica dust inhalation during tile and screed removal
Struck-by hazard from falling debris during tile stripping
Acute or chronic respiratory exposure if membrane contains asbestos (latent condition — unconfirmed)
Musculoskeletal strain from manual removal and debris handling
Dust generation affecting occupants in adjacent balconies and building interior
tasks.dominant_hazard: Acute respiratory exposure if asbestos-containing material present in failed membrane
controls: Wet all tile and screed surfaces with water spray before tool contact. Maintain dampness throughout removal — do not allow substrate to dry between passes.
Use dust extraction equipment with HEPA filter attached to all power tools. Position extraction nozzle within 300 mm of cutting or grinding point.
Erect full exclusion barrier around work area using heavy plastic sheeting and scaffold tie-points. Seal all gaps and penetrations to prevent dust escape to adjacent balconies.

Stop and visually check membrane substrate before removal. If membrane shows signs of lamination, friability, or age-pattern consistent with asbestos (see SDS and photographic guide), isolate area and tell project manager immediately.
Remove membrane manually with hand tools only. Do not grind, sand, or break membrane with power tools. Place removed membrane directly into sealed waste bags — do not drop or throw.
Brief all workers on asbestos recognition and reporting protocol before task starts. Display asbestos warning poster at work area entrance.
Stockpile all debris in rigid containers below scaffold. Cover containers with heavy plastic and tape seals. Do not allow loose debris to fall from height or accumulate on lower balconies.
Wear Class P2 mask/respirator (fit-tested) (not dust mask) during all removal work. Change filters after each shift or if resistance increases.
hold_points: ⚠️ HOLD POINT — do not start tile or screed removal until: site engineer has approved access scaffold, handover certificate has been signed, and exclusion barrier is fully erected and sealed

⚠️ HOLD POINT — do not proceed with membrane removal until: membrane substrate has been visually inspected for asbestos indicators and either confirmed safe to proceed with hand tools OR confirmed as suspected asbestos and isolate protocol triggered
stop_work: 🛑 STOP WORK if: wet suppression system fails, dust escapes exclusion barrier, or visible airborne dust is observed outside work area
🛑 STOP WORK if: membrane shows visual signs of friability, lamination, or suspected asbestos contamination
🛑 STOP WORK if: Class P2 respirators cannot be fitted properly or filters become blocked within shift
admin: Obtain site-specific asbestos recognition photographic guide or membrane product SDS before task start. Brief all workers on visual recognition.
Verify all workers hold current White Card (CPCCWHS1001) and working at heights competency (RIIOHS204E or equivalent).
Document membrane substrate condition in site diary. Photograph and retain SDS for any membrane product removed.
Arrange asbestos-licensed contractor contact and isolation procedure in case suspected asbestos is discovered during removal.
tell building occupants and adjacent balcony users of dust control measures and access restrictions before task starts.
ppe: Class P2 mask/respirator (fit-tested) (fitted and seal-tested before use each day)
Hard hat (required when working at height and below scaffold)

monitoring.critical_control: Verify wet suppression is active and dust extraction HEPA filter is in use at start of each removal pass
monitoring.frequency: Before each tool start and every 30 minutes during continuous removal work
monitoring.evidence: Visual confirmation of water spray on substrate, audible extraction fan, filter condition check, and photographic record if membrane damage or friability observed

responsibility.WKR: Perform Remove existing tile bed, screed, per SWMS

tasks.task: Expose substrate, investigate and document slab condition
tasks.scope: Clean exposed concrete slab surface; photograph and map all visible cracks, spalling, and delamination; document findings in site report; identify repair scope and mark for Leo and Associates inspection.
hazards: Silica dust inhalation during concrete surface cleaning
Contact dermatitis from cement dust and concrete alkalinity
Trip hazard from exposed slab edges, cracks, and cleaning debris
Respiratory irritation from dust migration into building interior
tasks.dominant_hazard: Silica dust inhalation during concrete cleaning operations
controls: Wet clean the exposed concrete surface using low-pressure water spray or damp cloth to suppress silica dust generation before photography and mapping commences.
Extract dust at source using HEPA-filtered vacuum or dust suppression unit during all cleaning operations; maintain continuous suction until surface is dry.
Wear P2 respirator (fit-tested, replacement cartridges on site) and disposable chemical-resistant gloves during all cleaning, photographing, and documentation work.
Barricade the exposed slab perimeter with high-visibility tape and 'Do Not Enter' signs to prevent occupant access and contain cleaning debris.
Lay protective ground sheets or tarps under the slab work area to contain dust-laden water runoff and prevent migration into building interior.
Complete photographic mapping of all visible cracks, spalling, and delamination using marked reference grid or scale card in each photograph.
Record all findings (location, size, depth, pattern) in a site defect report with dated photographs; flag areas requiring Leo and Associates structural inspection.
Sweep and damp-wipe the slab surface and surrounding area after cleaning is complete to remove residual dust before occupants re-enter zone.
hold_points: ⚠️ HOLD POINT — do not photograph or document slab until: wet cleaning is complete, dust extraction equipment is operational, and P2 respirators are fitted and verified on all workers
stop_work: 🛑 STOP WORK if: wet suppression or dust extraction fails, exposing workers or building interior to visible dust generation
🛑 STOP WORK if: slab condition reveals previously unknown structural damage, delamination depth, or load-bearing failure indicators — halt work and contact Leo and Associates immediately
admin: Confirm occupant notification has been issued before cleaning commences; obtain signed access permit from building manager.
Verify P2 respirators are fit-tested for each worker; maintain fit-test records on site.
Assign one worker as dust monitor; brief monitor on visible dust triggers and stop-work authority.
Photograph and geotag all defects in site report; cross-reference with Leo and Associates inspection scope.
Brief all workers on slab hazards (edge exposure, crack trip risk, dust containment) before work starts.
ppe: Hard hat (if working under scaffold or at slab level above occupied spaces)

monitoring.critical_control: Defect list reviewed and signed off by supervisor before rectification starts
monitoring.who: Designated dust monitor (worker assigned before shift start)
monitoring.frequency: Continuous during cleaning phase; pre-work suction check before each cleaning session
monitoring.evidence: Dust monitor checklist signed; extraction unit running log; P2 respirator fit-test record; site defect report with dated photographs and Leo and Associates flagged areas

responsibility.SUP: Supervise Expose substrate, investigate and document
responsibility.WKR: Perform Expose substrate, investigate and document per SWMS

tasks.task: Repair substrate cracks, spalling, and slab edges
tasks.scope: Grind crack edges and clean; apply epoxy injection or concrete repair mortar per engineer direction; reinstate slab edges and failed perimeter zones; allow cure time; prepare surface for primer.
hazards: Silica dust inhalation during concrete grinding
Chemical burn or respiratory irritation from epoxy or concrete repair mortar exposure
Contact dermatitis from uncured epoxy or mortar contact with skin
Noise exposure above 85 dB(A) during grinding operations
Trip hazard from repair materials, dust, and curing remnants on slab surface
tasks.dominant_hazard: Silica dust inhalation during concrete grinding and slab edge preparation
controls: Use wet grinding method — angle grinder with integral water suppression or wet-vac attachment — to suppress dust at source during crack edge and spalling preparation.
Wear respiratory protection (P2/P3 half-mask or powered air-fed) fitted to face and seal-checked before starting grinding — change cartridge or filter weekly or if odour detected.
Establish exclusion zone 4 m radius around grinding point — cordon with tape and sign — exclude occupants and unrelated workers during active dust generation.
Vacuum all residual dust using HEPA-filtered vacuum within 1 m of work surface immediately after grinding stops — do not dry sweep or air-blow.
Check SDS for epoxy or concrete repair mortar on point of use — confirm application temperature, cure time, and ventilation requirements before opening containers.
make sure slab surface is dry and clean of all dust, oil, and contaminants before applying epoxy injection or mortar — wipe with damp cloth if needed.
Apply epoxy or mortar only during suitable weather — temperature between 10–25 °C and relative humidity below 85 % — confirm with site thermometer before each application.
Ventilate cured repair area continuously during cure window — minimum 2 air changes per hour if indoors — keep window or door open or run portable fan.
hold_points: ⚠️ HOLD POINT — do not apply epoxy injection or mortar until: scaffold is erected, inspected, and handover certificate signed; exclusion zone is confirmed in place; substrate is dry, clean, and engineer-approved; SDS cure window and weather conditions are verified.

⚠️ HOLD POINT — do not apply primer or proceed to next stage until: repair surface has cured fully per SDS; defect inspection is complete and repair is confirmed sound; all dust and cured material remnants are removed; slab surface is dry and clean.
stop_work: 🛑 STOP WORK if: wet suppression fails, water pressure drops, or dust visible during grinding — do not resume until suppression system is repaired and tested.

🛑 STOP WORK if: ambient temperature falls below 10 °C or relative humidity exceeds 85 % — check weather forecast and site thermometer — do not resume application until conditions are within SDS range.
🛑 STOP WORK if: occupant or non-work personnel enters exclusion zone during active grinding or dust generation — evacuate work area immediately and reinstate cordon.
🛑 STOP WORK if: occupant balcony below work zone is not closed and barricaded

Record ambient temperature and relative humidity before each epoxy or mortar application — log in site diary.

Confirm engineer approval for repair method (epoxy injection vs. concrete mortar) and cure procedure before work starts.
Record cure completion time — mark slab with date/time of completion and expected traffic-ready time — communicate to building occupants.

Notify affected residents before any noise/dust generating work on their level or adjacent levels

eye protection— worn during grinding to protect eyes from water spray and rebound particles.

monitoring.frequency: Continuous during active grinding; before each application of epoxy or mortar; before cure completion.
monitoring.evidence: Visual inspection of water spray pattern; dust suppression maintained; thermometer and humidity meter readings logged; SDS cure time confirmed and marked on slab; defect inspection sign-off recorded.

tasks.task: Install screed, tile bed, and undertile membrane preparation
tasks.scope: Pour and level screed to design slopes and falls; allow cure; install undertile waterproofing membrane on screed; prepare tile bed to substrate and joint specifications.
hazards: Slip hazard on wet screed during pouring, levelling, and curing
Chemical burn or respiratory irritation from screed dust and additives
Musculoskeletal strain from manual screed application and levelling
Inadequate falls and slopes — ponding and water entrapment (workmanship hazard)
Trip hazard from screed curing debris and undertile membrane edges
tasks.dominant_hazard: Slip hazard on wet screed during application and curing phases
controls: Obtain SDS for screed product and waterproofing membrane before delivery; display on point of use.
Verify substrate is clean, dry, and free from laitance or contaminants before screed pouring starts.
Establish dedicated ventilation or natural air flow to prevent screed dust accumulation during mixing and application.
Contain screed mixing and application within barricaded area; restrict occupant and non-essential worker access during pour and cure phases.
Check all screed is applied and levelled to engineer-approved slopes and falls; no ponding or traps permitted.
Allow screed to cure for manufacturer-specified duration before membrane installation; verify cure by test patch or hardness check.
Install non-slip surface on all screed work areas during and after curing — tactile warning tape or slip-resistant coating.
Apply undertile waterproofing membrane per manufacturer method and environmental conditions; confirm weather window before application.
hold_points: ⚠️ HOLD POINT — do not install undertile membrane until: screed has cured to manufacturer specification and substrate is confirmed dry and level by site supervisor.
⚠️ HOLD POINT — do not start tiling until: waterproofing membrane cure is complete, all edges sealed, and tile bed adhesive environmental requirements (temperature, humidity) are met.
stop_work: 🛑 STOP WORK if: screed slopes or falls cannot be achieved to design specification or ponding is observed.
🛑 STOP WORK if: weather conditions fall outside membrane application window (temperature, humidity, wind) or substrate becomes contaminated.
🛑 STOP WORK if: screed dust or chemical irritant exposure symptoms occur or ventilation system fails during mixing or application.
admin: Brief all workers on SDS content for screed and membrane products before work starts.
Confirm scaffold handover certificate is signed and displayed before any elevated work begins.
Restrict building occupant access to work area during screed pouring, levelling, and membrane application.
Keep non-skid mats or warning tape on all screed surfaces until curing is complete.
Record screed cure time, membrane batch number, application date, and environmental conditions in site diary.
Verify working at heights permit is current and signed before elevated access is used.

Non-slip footwear with good grip (tested on wet screed surfaces).
Hard hat and high-visibility vest always on elevated work areas.
Hearing protection if mixing equipment noise exceeds 85 dB(A).

monitoring.who: Site supervisor and applicator (trained in product requirements).
monitoring.frequency: Before membrane application starts and continuously during application.
monitoring.evidence: Site diary record of cure duration, environmental conditions at time of application, and visual confirmation of dry substrate.

tasks.task: Install tiles, grout, and complete balcony surface finish
tasks.scope: Lay tiles to pattern and levels per design; grout joints and seal; install edge trim and upstands; reinstate sealant at building interfaces and balustrade bases.
hazards: Silica dust inhalation during tile cutting and grout preparation
Musculoskeletal strain from tile laying and repetitive grouting
Slip hazard on wet grout and curing tile surfaces
Chemical burn or respiratory irritation from grout and sealant fumes
Struck-by hazard from falling tiles during laying or edge trim installation
tasks.dominant_hazard: Silica dust inhalation during tile cutting and grout mixing operations
controls: Use wet cutting method for all tiles — water feed to blade, capture wet slurry in container, no dry breakout permitted.
Mix grout in sealed paddle mixer with dust extraction hood connected and running — no hand mixing or dry powder dispersal.
Wear respiratory protection — P2 mask/respirator (fit-tested) minimum during cutting; P3 cartridge mask during grout mixing and joint preparation.
Provide general ventilation across work area — open adjacent doors/windows and position fan to push dust away from workers and building interior.
Barricade wet tile and grout surfaces with hazard tape — post 'Wet Floor — Slip Hazard' sign at balcony entry, maintain until surfaces cure.
Store tile stacks on stable base with restraint straps — no overhanging tiles, maximum 5 tiles per stack at edge locations.
Install edge trim only after tile adhesive cure confirmed per product SDS — hold substrate for 24–48 hours minimum before trim traffic load.
Apply sealant only when substrate temperature and humidity within product SDS window — check and record conditions before and after application.
hold_points: ⚠️ HOLD POINT — do not start tile laying until: scaffold handover certificate signed by licenced scaffolder and working at heights permit approved and posted on site.

⚠️ HOLD POINT — do not install edge trim or upstands until: site supervisor confirms tile adhesive fully cured per manufacturer SDS (typically 24–48 hours) and substrate checked for voids or movement.
stop_work: 🛑 STOP WORK if: wet cutting dust suppression fails, water feed to blade stops, or dust extraction hood is disconnected or damaged during use.
🛑 STOP WORK if: grout or sealant fumes cause respiratory irritation, dizziness, or headache in any worker — move to fresh air immediately, do not restart until ventilation confirmed adequate.
🛑 STOP WORK if: wet tile or grout surfaces are disturbed by building occupants or unauthorized personnel — reinstall barricade and slip hazard signage, reset cure timer if surface contaminated.
🛑 STOP WORK if: occupant balcony below work zone is not closed and barricaded
admin: Confirm EPA licence current and posted on site before grout and sealant delivery.
Obtain and post working at heights permit signed by competent authority — must be visible at work area.
Verify all workers hold White Card (CPCCWHS1001) — induction record on file before starting.
Verify working at heights competency — RIIOHS204E or equivalent current, record checked and filed.
Request and review tile and grout product SDS — confirm chemical hazards, cure times, temperature/humidity windows, first aid response, and make sure SDS available at point of use.
Confirm noise management plan in place if cutting generates >85 dB — coordinate timing with building occupant management if residential.
Record scaffold handover certificate and all relevant permits and competency checks in site induction folder.
Provide written briefing on wet cutting containment and grout mixing procedure — worker sign-off on toolbox talk record.
ppe: P2 respiratory protection mask (tile cutting operations)
P3 cartridge mask (grout mixing and joint preparation)
High-visibility vest or tabard (scaffolding work at height)
Hard hat (striking hazard from scaffold or falling materials)

monitoring.who: Supervisor and tile layer (pre-cut check); Supervisor (continuous during mixing)
monitoring.frequency: Before each cutting session; each grout batch prepared; continuous during work hour
monitoring.evidence: Visual observation of water flow and extraction hood operation; wet slurry visible in capture container; absence of visible dust cloud at cutting location; grout mixer hood intake clear of blockage; worker respiratory protection worn and fitted correctly throughout.

tasks.task: Apply primer and install new waterproofing membrane system
tasks.scope: Apply specified primer to prepared substrate; install waterproofing membrane per system schedule; treat seams, penetrations, and edges; install secondary protection layer; allow full cure before testing.
hazards: Respiratory irritation or chemical burn from primer vapours and fumes
Contact dermatitis or skin burn from primer or membrane contact
Slip hazard on wet or cured primer and membrane surfaces
Environmental release or vapour migration affecting occupants in adjacent areas
Inadequate cure time before secondary layer application — membrane failure
tasks.dominant_hazard: Respiratory irritation or chemical burn from primer and membrane system exposure
controls: Obtain and display Safety Data Sheet (SDS) for primer and membrane system at point of use before application starts.
Ventilate work area continuously — open windows and doors on both sides of work zone; use portable fan to direct vapours away from occupied areas.
Check substrate is dry, clean, and free of dust, grease, and loose material before primer application — damp-wipe residual dust if needed.
Apply primer only to the prepared area using specified application method — do not apply in high winds or rain.
Prohibit entry to work area and adjacent occupied zones during primer application and for 2 hours after; post 'Do Not Enter — Chemical Work in Progress' signs.
Install waterproofing membrane per manufacturer's schedule — align seams, overlap edges per specification, and treat all penetrations and flashings before secondary layer.
Allow primer and membrane to cure for full time specified on SDS and product schedule before secondary protection layer is applied — do not compress cure window.
Wipe up spills immediately with absorbent material; place in sealed container and remove from site.
hold_points: ⚠️ HOLD POINT — do not apply membrane until: substrate is signed off by supervising waterproofer as dry, clean, and primer fully cured per SDS.
stop_work: 🛑 STOP WORK if: ventilation fails, fume odour reaches adjacent occupied areas, or wind exceeds 5 m/s during application.
🛑 STOP WORK if: primer or membrane cannot be applied within SDS environmental limits (temperature, humidity, rain risk).
🛑 STOP WORK if: substrate condition changes — unexpected moisture, contamination, or structural crack discovered during prep or application.
🛑 STOP WORK if: occupant balcony below work zone is not closed and barricaded
admin: Confirm occupants of adjacent areas have been notified of chemical work and fume risk 24 hours before start.
Record SDS location, product batch numbers, and application start/cure window completion date on site log.
Brief workers on fume direction, escape routes, and emergency contact before each shift.
Obtain written confirmation from building occupant or supervisor that adjacent areas have been ventilated and occupants are not affected before secondary layer application.
Close and barricade balconies directly below active work zone before elevated work starts each day

task_blocks_raw.task: Repair substrate cracks, spalling, and slab edges

hazards: Silica dust inhalation during concrete grinding
Chemical burn or respiratory irritation from epoxy or concrete repair mortar exposure
Contact dermatitis from uncured epoxy or mortar contact with skin
Noise exposure above 85 dB(A) during grinding operations
Trip hazard from repair materials, dust, and curing remnants on slab surface
task_blocks_raw.dominant_hazard: Silica dust inhalation during concrete grinding and slab edge preparation
controls: Use wet grinding method — angle grinder with integral water suppression or wet-vac attachment — to suppress dust at source during crack edge and spalling preparation.
Wear respiratory protection (P2/P3 half-mask or powered air-fed) fitted to face and seal-checked before starting grinding — change cartridge or filter weekly or if odour detected.
Establish exclusion zone 4 m radius around grinding point — cordon with tape and sign — exclude occupants and unrelated workers during active dust generation.
Vacuum all residual dust using HEPA-filtered vacuum within 1 m of work surface immediately after grinding stops — do not dry sweep or air-blow.
Check SDS for epoxy or concrete repair mortar on point of use — confirm application temperature, cure time, and ventilation requirements before opening containers.
make sure slab surface is dry and clean of all dust, oil, and contaminants before applying epoxy injection or mortar — wipe with damp cloth if needed.
Apply epoxy or mortar only during suitable weather — temperature between 10–25 °C and relative humidity below 85 % — confirm with site thermometer before each application.
Ventilate cured repair area continuously during cure window — minimum 2 air changes per hour if indoors — keep window or door open or run portable fan.

task_blocks_raw.dominant_hazard: Fall from height or struck-by injury during scaffold dismantling
controls: Obtain signed handover certificate from licenced scaffolder before any dismantling commences.
Establish exclusion zone 2m radius below scaffold during dismantling — barricade and post spotters at ground level.
Dismantle scaffold in reverse sequence of erection — follow engineer-approved method statement with no unauthorised sequence changes.
Check all scaffold ties, braces, and base pads remain secure before starting each dismantling phase — stop work immediately if movement detected.
Lower all scaffold components to ground using manual handling or equipment — prohibit throwing or dropping components.
Use damp cloth method to clean building exterior and common areas — wet-sweep floors to suppress dust affecting occupants.
Restrict access to occupied building areas during cleaning — use separate entry/exit routes for workers and residents.
Confirm all plant removal routes are clear of pedestrians and vehicles — use spotters and reversing beepers during plant egress.
hold_points: ⚠️ HOLD POINT — do not start scaffold dismantling until: licenced scaffolder has signed handover certificate and confirmed all load conditions have been satisfied.
⚠️ HOLD POINT — do not hand over building to manager until: final inspection complete, all defects recorded or remediated, all debris removed, and cleaning finished to occupant-safe standard.
stop_work: 🛑 STOP WORK if: any scaffold component movement, loosening, or collapse is observed during dismantling.
🛑 STOP WORK if: exclusion zone is breached by pedestrians, residents, or vehicles during dismantling.
🛑 STOP WORK if: dust suppression fails during exterior cleaning and dust is entering occupied building areas.
admin: Brief all workers on dismantling sequence and exclusion zone boundaries before work starts.
Assign one supervisor to monitor scaffold dismantling and make sure spotters remain in place below work area.
Record final inspection findings and defect list — provide copy to building manager at handover.
Confirm EPA licence compliance if triggered by scope of cleaning activity — tell EPA if required.
Arrange traffic control for plant removal egress if site egress crosses public roads or shared carpark.
Provide building manager with photographic record of final condition before plant demobilisation.
ppe: Dust mask or respirator (if creating dust during cleaning)
